analysis.title: GS Wilson - Weekly Mash 16 Oct 2026
key_insights: Wilson attributes the week's sharpest price moves to two catalysts: reported comments from CoreWeave co-founder McBee in the FT on insurers' 'unlimited' capital availability, and a more urgent debate on frontier-lab business models and closed vs open model competition.
GS credit research says AI-related corporate bonds from neoclouds or with frontier lab exposure are at the epicentre of the funding cost debate.

Wilson expects the frontier-lab debate to become more tightly defined and more transparent in coming weeks. Market projections of capex intensity, funding needs, credit quality and where value is captured in AI will be re-appraised as it evolves.

Wilson argues the fixed income trend break this week should not be read as a binary change in the AI narrative. Second derivatives of capex and earnings growth likely slow, but the AI investment mega-theme is intact, and prices already reflect the slowdown.

Wilson sees no evidence of slowing compute demand or compute pricing. He cites OpenAI's Sarah Friar saying compute bought a year ago could be sold today for 3 to 5x and that the company is still short compute.

Wilson reiterates that through Q3 earnings the biggest AI spenders will likely show ROI, continue to self-fund spending, and stay relatively immune to the value-capture debate. Leadership is flipping from AI spend beneficiaries to the biggest AI investors.
Bonds rallied and broke the precipitous sell-off this week. Bonds could not sell off further after CPI/PPI and yields broke lower Thursday, which Wilson reads as exhaustion.
Below the index level, Nasdaq fell 1.5% on Wednesday while S&P ex-AI and Europe rose and outperformed NDX by more than 200bps.
GS upgraded bonds to Overweight for the coming 12 months on Monday. Wilson expects the focus on rates to persist because energy price pressures have not broken lower.

Momentum (price, positioning, sentiment) has been abruptly negative since end of Q2. Wilson thinks the pendulum may have swung too far from a realistic central scenario, with neocloud credit bearishness at the centre.

GS Prime data: Asia fundamental L/S down 7% this month and +16% YTD (from +40% in June). TMT L/S -5% MTD, +12% YTD (from +24% in June). Global Fundamental L/S -2% MTD, +10% YTD (from +17%). Europe L/S flat MTD, +8% YTD.
Global AI stocks (GSXGGLAI) were sold for a 6th straight day, and the cumulative position reduction over 6 sessions is as extreme as anything since the launch of ChatGPT.

The 'AI winners' vs 'AI-at-risk' trade broke at end of June after being up 90%+ for the year and has since halved. The equity momentum factor behaves the same, and both are retesting lows after a September bounce.
CoreWeave is testing its July lows, and Wilson flags a possible break lower next week amid broader tech weakness.
Wilson was surprised how modest USD IG and HY issuance estimates are for this year and next, citing Amanda Lynam's report 'AI, Credit, and a Higher Cost of Capital'.

On 2027 equity supply, GS (Snider) says net supply of US public equity, including expiring lockups, will likely rise next year by the most since 2000. Issuance would still be well under 1% of market cap. Wilson says the 1990s show elevated supply did not block gains when the market believed proceeds funded productive deployment.

tension_points.bull_case: Wilson says the AI mega-theme is intact, with no evidence of slowing compute demand or pricing, biggest spenders self-funding and showing ROI in Q3, and prices already reflecting slower capex growth.
tension_points.bear_case: GS credit research puts neocloud and frontier-lab bonds at the epicentre of a funding cost debate, and a financing accident or weaker growth drove AI equities lower this week.
